memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So he had his chariot made ready and took his army with him. He took six
hundred of the best chariots, along with all the other chariots of Egypt, with
officers over all of them." - Ex 14:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Egypt brings out everything. Six hundred elite chariots, plus every other
chariot in the country, with commanders over all of them.

Chariots were the most advanced military technology of the age. Against a crowd
of former slaves on foot, with women, children, livestock and baggage, this was
not a contest. It was a formality.

It is worth being honest that from a human point of view Israel had no answer to
this. None. No weapons that mattered, no training, no escape route, no
possibility.

That is often precisely the setting God chooses. Gideon's army was cut down to
three hundred so that Israel could not claim credit (Judg 7:2). David went out
with a sling. Paul said God's power is made perfect in weakness (2 Cor 12:9).

Psalm 20:7 puts it beautifully: "Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but
we trust in the name of the LORD our God." The psalmist is not pretending
chariots are ineffective. He is saying there is something stronger.

Whatever is bearing down on you today, count it honestly. Then remember who is
on the other side of the ledger.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are the "chariots" currently bearing down on your life?
2. Where are you quietly trusting in resources rather than in God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I see clearly what is against me. Help me to see even more clearly who is
for me. I trust in Your name, not in my resources. Amen.
